title.zh: CPU 是怎么猜着往前跑的

desc.zh: 一条分支要等十几拍才知道往哪走，CPU 却不等：它先猜，猜对了白赚，猜错了推倒重来。它怎么猜得这么准？为什么一颗 CPU 能同时有几百条指令在路上？这种猜测又为什么会泄露秘密？十个模型：1 位与 2 位计数器、排序数组、gshare、TAGE、返回栈、超标量、寄存器重命名与重排序缓冲、窗口大小、Spectre 的玩具机器。
desc.en: A branch takes a dozen cycles to resolve, and a CPU does not wait: it guesses, gains when right and starts over when wrong. How does it guess so well? Why can one CPU have hundreds of instructions in flight? And why does the guessing leak secrets? Ten models: 1-bit and 2-bit counters, the sorted array, gshare, TAGE, the return stack, superscalar issue, renaming and the reorder buffer, window size, and a toy machine for Spectre.

title.en: Why a wrong guess costs more on a wide core

desc.zh: 一次猜错要扔掉的是「拍数 × 每拍条数」：Zen 5 约 15 拍、每拍 8 条，95% 的准确率就丢掉一半以上的时间。
desc.en: A wrong guess throws away cycles × width: about 15 cycles at 8 per cycle on Zen 5, so 95% accuracy loses more than half the time.

title.zh: 1 位与 2 位饱和计数器、排序数组为什么快
title.en: 1-bit and 2-bit counters; why the sorted array is faster

desc.zh: 2 位计数器要错两次才改主意，循环出口只错一次；排好序的数组让 if 变得可猜，无分支写法则根本不猜。
desc.en: A 2-bit counter needs two misses to change its mind, so a loop exit costs one miss; sorting makes the if predictable, and branchless code does not guess at all.

zh: 为什么排序后的数组处理更快
en: why is processing a sorted array faster

desc.zh: 把最近几条分支的结果和地址异或起来查表，相关的分支就能互相提示；表太小时历史越长反而越乱。
desc.en: XOR the outcomes of recent branches with the address to index the table, so correlated branches inform each other; in a small table longer history only dilutes it.

desc.zh: 几张表各用几何级数长度的历史并带标记，最长的命中说了算；同样存储下比 gshare 准。
desc.en: Several tagged tables with geometric history lengths; the longest hit decides, and at equal storage it beats gshare.

zh: 现代 CPU 怎么做分支预测

title.zh: 分支目标缓冲与返回地址栈
title.en: Branch target buffer and return address stack

desc.zh: 方向猜对还不够，还要知道跳到哪：BTB 记目标，返回栈记函数返回地址，栈不够深就开始猜错。
desc.en: Direction is not enough; the target must be known too: the BTB remembers targets and the return stack return addresses, which go wrong when calls nest deeper than the stack.

desc.zh: 每拍能发几条取决于指令之间的依赖；按顺序发射时宽了也用不上，乱序才吃得到并行。
desc.en: How many instructions issue per cycle depends on dependences between them; in-order issue cannot use extra width, out-of-order can.

title.zh: 乱序执行与寄存器重命名

desc.zh: 把架构寄存器改名到物理寄存器，假依赖（WAR、WAW）消失，只剩真依赖；准备好的指令先走。
desc.en: Renaming architectural registers onto physical ones removes false dependences (WAR, WAW), leaving only true ones; ready instructions go first.

title.zh: 重排序缓冲与精确异常
title.en: The reorder buffer and precise exceptions

desc.zh: 乱序执行、按序提交：ROB 从头部按顺序认账，猜错或出错时把后面的全部作废，程序看起来像一条条执行。
desc.en: Execute out of order, commit in order: the ROB retires from its head, and on a mispredict or fault everything younger is discarded, so the program appears sequential.

title.en: How big the out-of-order window is

desc.zh: Zen 5 448、Lion Cove 576：窗口越大越能藏住缓存缺失，但每几百条就有一次猜错，窗口再大也填不满。
desc.en: Zen 5 448, Lion Cove 576: a bigger window hides more cache misses, but with a mispredict every few hundred instructions it never fills.

title.zh: Spectre：猜测为什么会泄露秘密

desc.zh: 猜错的指令结果被扔掉，但它们读过的缓存行留下了；用页面里的玩具机器看越界读怎样经由计时泄露，以及 lfence 和下标掩码怎么堵。
desc.en: Results of wrongly guessed instructions are discarded, but the cache lines they touched remain; a toy machine on the page shows how an out-of-bounds read leaks through timing, and how lfence and index masking stop it.

title.zh: 分支预测与推测执行的前沿（截至 2026 年 11 月）
title.en: The frontier of prediction and speculation (as of November 2026)

desc.zh: 新的预测器还在比赛，新的推测执行漏洞还在出现：Branch Privilege Injection、Branch Target Reuse，以及它们的补丁代价。
desc.en: New predictors still compete and new speculation flaws keep appearing: Branch Privilege Injection, Branch Target Reuse, and what their fixes cost.

title.zh: 看一段代码时问三件事
title.en: Three questions about a piece of code

desc.zh: 分支能不能猜、依赖链有多长、缺失能不能重叠。
desc.en: Can its branches be predicted, how long are its dependence chains, can its misses overlap.

zh: 怎么减少分支预测失败
